text:
maya: Heads up — saw repeated OOMs on prod-serving for llama-70b-8k during large-chat workloads after yesterday's kernel-selector change (commit a1b2c3f). Logs show scratchpad/logits ballooning.

jonah: can you paste the top of the logs + profiler? which host/replica?

maya: replica r-5 in us-west-2, pod gpu-3. Log tail:
```
E OOM: allocation failed for logits_scratchpad 1.2GB
AllocatorState: free=0, slabs=[...], frag=42%
Stack: runtime::alloc_logit_scratch
```

ryan: ran quick memtrace with nvprof + our mem-analyzer. Snapshot: peak 48GB, resident 40GB, fragmentation 38%. Most large live buffers were 'activation-accum' and 'logits_scratchpad'. Screenshot: https://files.internal/redwood/perf/2681234567/snap.png

cassandra: looks like the kernel-selector change bumped sequence-length optimized kernels which allocate bigger temporary KV workspaces for concat paths. Could be interplay with freelist compaction frequency.

phil: Is this a regression vs last week? any canary failures earlier?

maya: Yes — before deploy peak ~36GB. After deploy it's +12GB and unstable. Canary had a single minor fail but we didn't escalate.

jonah: hypothesis: our allocator's small-slab sizing made many medium allocations fall into new 'large' path, increasing external fragmentation. Two quick mitigations: 1) enable eager-free for logits scratchpad after token emit 2) bump slab-granularity for affected model while we test.

ryan: pprof snippet:
```
heap_objects_by_size:
  64MB: 12
  8MB: 120
  256KB: 400
largest_free_segment: 6MB
estimated_waste: 9.6GB
```

cassandra: also KV cache pinning is causing some sticky allocations; if prefix-aware warmup touches large KV ranges, we should evict cold entries earlier. Suggest adding 'kv.pinned_threshold=0.1' for unstable model rollout.

jonah: I'll push a hotfix to runtime to (a) add eager-free flag for logits (b) temporarily increase slab_min from 4MB -> 8MB for llama-70b-8k. Keeping change scoped to model-tag. Rolling canary.

maya: thanks. Also add an opt-in telemetry metric 'slab_frag_pct' and 'logits_peak_bytes' so we can alert earlier.

infra-bot: deploy started: hotfix/2681234567 -> canary us-west-2 (3 replicas)

jonah: canary logs so far: peak 39GB, frag 19% — initial good sign. Will monitor 30m.

ryan: note for follow-up perf work: run kernel-replay test with longest sequence distribution and run batcher stress to measure continuous batching growth. I think batching heuristics also interact — larger batches increase temporary logits workspace.

phil: please capture experiment notes + perf graphs in the thread — schedule retrospective with runtime team tomorrow.

maya: will update with metrics. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
